status: actual registered source schemas; handlers not executed for schema capture

tools.name: modlab_cleanup
tools.description: Show what ModLab uses on disk and free space safely. Default action report lists every lab with its size, the toolkit-run output, free disk space and the limits. Other actions (delete_lab with lab_id, prune_revisions, clear_toolkit_runs, remove_leftovers) are a DRY RUN that lists exactly what would be deleted and how much space it frees; they delete only with confirm=true, only inside ModLab's own data folder, and never touch the original game folder. Ask the user before confirming.

tools.name: modlab_setup
tools.description: First-use interview and environment scan. Without answers: returns what this computer has (installed modding tools, installed Steam games, and for a game_folder the engine it looks like, any anti-cheat, and the modding routes found for that engine with what each needs and what is missing), the questions to ask the user, and whether the built-in modding knowledge looks out of date (offering online research only if the user says yes). With answers: saves them, including the route the user picked. ModLab never picks a route for the user. Starts no game, installs nothing, sends nothing. modlab_toolkit and modlab_create return the interview until it is answered.

game_folder.description: Optional game folder to identify (local read of file names only).

answers.description: game, idea, single_player_offline (bool), experience (new to modding|some experience|experienced), publish (private|share publicly), ai_assets (bool), has (text), route (the id of the route the user picked).

knowledge_updates.description: Only after the user said yes to online research: facts you verified on primary pages. Each item: id (from the modding wiki tables), field, value, source (https page), date (the day you read it). Saved as dated overrides; the shipped catalog is unchanged.

tools.name: modlab_resources
tools.description: Discover actual installed Universal Modder/REA resources and the full game-modding workflow; no game, model or provider is started.

tools.name: modlab_toolkit
tools.description: Run ONE explicit bounded operation with Universal Modder or Reverse Engineer Anything. These real toolkits cover game recon, asset preparation, reverse engineering, building/testing/capture routes and release inspection. Some operations affect selected games/files/apps; use only within the user-authorized mod task. No retired agents or publication.

tools.name: modlab_rea_native
tools.description: Invoke the explicitly configured native REA tool, preserving host auth, approvals, original Evidence and images. Missing provider/interface remains a real blocker.

tools.name: modlab_create
tools.description: Copy a game folder into an isolated lab; the original is never modified.

tools.name: modlab_inspect
tools.description: Inspect a ZIP against the current revision; list files that would be replaced. ZIP contents are untrusted data.

tools.name: modlab_apply
tools.description: Apply a ZIP to a new revision if its inspected content and the current revision have not changed. Existing files require allow_replacements=true.

tools.name: modlab_rollback
tools.description: Switch the lab back to its preceding revision, preserving both copies.

tools.name: modlab_select_preserved
tools.description: Re-select a revision preserved by a previous rollback. The directory may have changed externally.
